scope: Auto Live force-perfect state transitions for normal, Flick, Long, and Slide notes

flick: NoteFlickBase inherits NoteSingleBase.MoveState and its adjusted root crossing
the override then obtains a synthetic Flick X position and dispatches the Flick movement callback with Perfect (4)
long: root crossing changes state and submits front Perfect
forcePerfectOnUpdate samples adjusted music position against the Long terminal position
terminal crossing judges the linked after note and Long root as Perfect
slide: forcePerfectMoveState samples adjusted music position and submits front Perfect at the root crossing
forcePerfectOnUpdate operates on the current pending after note
an intermediate crossing submits Perfect for that intermediate node
the terminal route submits Perfect after the pending terminal crossing
forcePerfectStopState separately submits Perfect for the selected stopped after note

prototype.slide_update_limit: one pending intermediate or terminal transition per note object per update
prototype.particle_order: advance existing particle simulations before resolving current note crossings

confirmed: Auto Live routes Long and Slide away from ordinary input judgement into type-specific force-perfect methods.
Long and Slide root force-perfect methods compare adjusted music position with their root absolute position before submitting Perfect.
Long terminal and Slide pending after-note force-perfect routes compare adjusted music position with the corresponding terminal or after-node position.
Slide forcePerfectOnUpdate operates on a selected pending after note rather than judging the entire remaining Slide in one call.
NoteFlickBase.forcePerfect reuses NoteSingleBase.forcePerfect and then dispatches its specialized synthetic Flick movement path with Perfect.
inference: The portable one-transition-per-note-per-update rule preserves the recovered call granularity when a backend update skips across multiple Slide nodes.
unresolved: The exact Unity ordering between the base Perfect submission and specialized Flick synthetic movement callback is not reproduced as two portable judgement events.
The portable update ordering is deterministic but does not claim exact Unity PlayerLoop scheduling.
Exact animation callback timing and per-node Unity object activation order remain outside this backend-neutral state model.
